title: Spotify Music Streaming: Complete Architecture
description: Design a global music streaming platform with gapless audio streaming, Spotify Connect device sync, collaborative filtering, and royalty tracking.

data.text: Design a music and audio streaming service at Spotify scale. The platform serves 600+ million monthly active users listening to a catalog of 100+ million tracks and 5 million podcasts. Core technical demands include sub-200ms audio startup with gapless crossfade transitions, multi-device playback synchronization (Spotify Connect), offline encrypted playback, daily personalized discovery feeds (Discover Weekly), and fault-tolerant play tracking for artist royalty payouts.

terms.definition: Client buffers the first 30 seconds of the upcoming queue track in background memory while the current track finishes, delivering 0ms transition delay.
A state-synchronization protocol maintaining active playback state (track, position, volume) across phones, laptops, and smart speakers via WebSockets.
Matrix factorization analyzing user playlist co-occurrences and listening habits to find latent music preference representations.
Spotify's open-source C++ library for ultra-fast vector similarity search over high-dimensional song and user embeddings.
Royalty rules requiring a song to play continuously for at least 30 seconds before logging an immutable event for financial settlement.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Audio Playback: Stream high-fidelity audio (96, 160, 320 kbps Ogg Vorbis/AAC) with instant startup
Lookahead Queue & Playlists: Manage dynamic play queues, collaborative playlists, and personal libraries
Spotify Connect: Seamlessly transfer and control playback across devices (Phone -> Smart Speaker / TV)
Search: Low-latency search across tracks, artists, albums, lyrics, and user-generated playlists
Personalized Discovery: Algorithmic playlists (Discover Weekly, Release Radar, Daily Mix) generated periodically
Royalty & Analytics Logging: Track streaming seconds to pay rights holders and power Spotify Wrapped

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Scale: 600M+ active users; 100M+ songs; 50M+ concurrent audio streams at peak hours
Startup Latency: Audio begins playing within 200ms of clicking Play (<50ms on warm client cache)
Availability: 99.99% for audio playback and catalog metadata browsing
Bandwidth Optimization: 50%+ of daily plays served from client local disk cache and edge CDNs
Royalty Auditability: 100% durable event logging for tracks played >30 seconds

data.text: The system segregates low-latency audio delivery (CDN + Client Cache) from metadata microservices (Cassandra / Postgres) and the heavy offline recommendation pipeline (Hadoop / Spark / Annoy).

data.text: To achieve zero stutter and instant track changes, the client checks local encrypted storage first, fetches the current song via HTTP Range requests from the nearest CDN PoP, and automatically buffers the beginning of the next track.

data.caption: Audio streaming and lookahead prefetch sequence with 30-second royalty threshold reporting
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as 👤 Listener
    participant App as 📱 Spotify App
    participant Cache as 💾 Local Disk Cache
    participant CDN as 🌍 Audio CDN
    participant S3 as 🗃️ Audio S3 Vault
    participant Kafka as 📨 Kafka Royalty Queue

    User->>App: Clicks "Play" on Track 1 (Song A)
    App->>Cache: Check if Song A cached locally
    alt Cache Hit (50% of plays)
        Cache-->>App: Read decrypted audio stream from disk
        App->>App: Audio playback starts in <20ms
    else Cache Miss
        App->>CDN: GET /audio/Song_A.ogg (HTTP Range: bytes 0-131072)
        alt CDN Hit
            CDN-->>App: Return initial 128KB audio chunk (<80ms)
        else CDN Miss
            CDN->>S3: Fetch audio file from origin
            S3-->>CDN: Audio binary stream
            CDN-->>App: Stream audio bytes to player
        end
        App->>Cache: Save chunks to local LRU cache
    end

    Note over App: Song A reaches 30 seconds mark
    App->>Kafka: Emit "TrackPlayed30s" Event (Eligible for Royalty)

    Note over App: Song A is 80% finished (Lookahead Prefetch)
    App->>CDN: GET /audio/Song_B.ogg (HTTP Range: bytes 0-262144)
    CDN-->>App: Buffer first 30s of Song B in memory
    Note over App: Song A finishes -> Instant 0ms Crossfade to Song B!

faqs.question: Why does Spotify use Ogg Vorbis instead of MP3 or pure AAC?
faqs.answer: Ogg Vorbis is an open-source, royalty-free audio codec that provides significantly better perceptual audio quality than MP3 at equivalent bitrates (especially at 160kbps and 320kbps). Avoiding per-decoder patent licensing fees saves millions of dollars annually while delivering superior sound fidelity.

faqs.question: How does Spotify Connect transfer playback between devices instantaneously?
faqs.answer: All active player devices hold persistent WebSockets to the Connect Gateway. The active state (TrackID, exact Millisecond Offset, Play/Pause state) is stored in Redis. When you press "Switch to Living Room Speaker", your phone sends a command; the gateway updates Redis and pushes a "StartPlayback(TrackID, offset)" payload to the speaker socket within 50ms.

faqs.question: How does Discover Weekly generate 600 million unique playlists every Monday?
faqs.answer: Discover Weekly relies on offline batch collaborative filtering (ALS) run on Apache Spark clusters over the weekend. User listening histories and 4+ billion public playlists are factorized into latent 100-dimensional vector embeddings. Spotify's Annoy library finds vector neighbors in sub-milliseconds to compile 30 tailored recommendations per user.

faqs.question: Why is client-side disk caching critical for streaming economics?
faqs.answer: Streaming audio from edge CDNs costs bandwidth fees per gigabyte. Most music listeners repeat their favorite 50-100 songs daily. Spotify reserves up to 10GB of encrypted storage on mobile and desktop disks as an LRU cache. Over 50% of all music played never touches the internet, drastically cutting CDN transit bills.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Lookahead prefetching buffers upcoming tracks in advance to guarantee 0ms gapless playback transitions
Client local encrypted caching absorbs >50% of track playbacks without hitting CDN networks
Spotify Connect orchestrates multi-device remote control via persistent full-duplex WebSockets and Redis
Implicit collaborative filtering paired with vector search (Annoy) drives Discover Weekly at global scale
Stream reporting enforces a strict 30-second threshold before emitting auditable royalty events to Kafka
data.takeaway: Spotify achieves instantaneous, seamless audio experiences through client-side lookahead buffering and local caching, while centralized WebSocket gateways power effortless cross-device playback control.
